name: Deeply integrated capability withdrawal and decommission planning

defaults.system: You are a bounded software-planning agent. Do not write implementation code. Do not invent missing facts, permissions, files, frameworks, or product decisions. Return exactly one JSON object with no Markdown fence or surrounding prose. For a PLAN request use: {"response_type":"plan","status":"ready|blocked","requirements":[{"id":"R1","interpretation":"..."}],"assumptions":["..."],"blocking_questions":["..."],"affected_components":["..."],"steps":[{"id":"P1","objective":"...","requirement_ids":["R1"],"dependencies":[],"verification":["..."]}],"risks":[{"risk":"...","mitigation":"..."}],"verification_strategy":["..."]}. For a TASK_SET request use: {"response_type":"task_set","status":"ready|blocked","source_plan_status":"ready|blocked","requirement_ids":["R1"],"blocking_questions":["..."],"tasks":[{"id":"T1","objective":"...","requirement_ids":["R1"],"scope":{"include":["..."],"exclude":["..."]},"dependencies":[],"implementation_work":["..."],"acceptance_criteria":["..."],"tests":["..."],"worker_instruction":"..."}]}. Declare every supplied requirement ID exactly once in requirements or requirement_ids. Every ready step/task must trace to supplied IDs; dependencies must reference earlier items. Use at most seven steps or tasks. If essential authority or information is missing, set status blocked, ask precise questions, and return no implementation steps/tasks.

cases.prompt: PLAN only. Four iterations into an existing desktop asset-management application, the product owner has explicitly withdrawn the unreleased predictive-maintenance scheduling capability. It is wired into a dashboard, domain service, shared background queue, SQLite persistence, internal REST endpoints, configuration, tests, and documentation. Other released capabilities use the same queue, database, reporting utilities, and authentication and must remain intact. Requirements: R1 record the original capability requirement as withdrawn and mark queued work that depends on it superseded or cancelled before assigning new work; R2 make a forward decommission change from the repository's current state rather than blindly reverting historical commits that contain unrelated work; R3 inventory entry points, consumers, stored state, endpoints, configuration, tests, documentation, and cross-feature dependencies before removal; R4 stage the change by stopping new invocations, creating or using a clean boundary, detaching consumers, removing capability-specific implementation, and then cleaning residual artifacts; R5 preserve all shared infrastructure and verify every released workflow that uses it; R6 do not automatically destroy stored records, schema objects, or migration history—place any irreversible data cleanup in a separate approval-gated proposal; R7 the feature has no external consumers, but migrate all internal callers before removing its internal endpoints; R8 preserve small reviewable commits and an explicit rollback point until validation passes; R9 prove absence through reference searches and negative user journeys, and prove preservation through full regression tests and checks for orphaned jobs, configuration, and data access. Produce the required plan JSON.

TASK_SET only. Convert the preceding decommission plan into bounded, dependency-ordered task contracts covering R1-R9. Make plan invalidation, impact inventory, invocation shutdown, consumer detachment, capability removal, residual cleanup, and independent validation separately reviewable where practical. Keep irreversible stored-data cleanup outside authorized implementation work.
